title: Canonicalize mesh-node output to ArrayMesh (HalfEdgeMesh stays internal)
description:
Currently the DSL node ecosystem is split on its output type: 23 nodes return HalfEdgeMesh, 4 return ArrayMesh. 3 nodes already produce both depending on input. The mixed output has two visible consequences:

  1. Patch overlay in the mesh viewer (VIEW-7) works on OBJ-loaded meshes (always ArrayMesh) but not on DSL-generated meshes — the decomposer requires a flat triangle list and a HalfEdgeMesh compiled-surface uses a different vertex ordering than the boolean mask indices we'd install as tags. User reported: 'I thought all of our nodes used array mesh since halfEdgeMesh has problems with OOM, if that is not true we need to fix it'.
  2. Downstream consumers (viewer EBO, exporter, mesh_compare, patch decomposer, auto_segment) have to special-case which kind of mesh they got.

## Survey

### HalfEdgeMesh-returning nodes (23)
- curve: BiRailLoftNode, BirailLoftMeshNode, CurveSweepMeshNode, CurveToMeshNode
- geometry: MeshBooleanNode, SeparateGeometryNode
- modifier: ApplyBoneNode, AttachToSurfaceNode, ExtrudeMeshNode*, InsetFacesNode*, InstanceOnPointsNode, MirrorGeometryNode, SpherizeMeshNode, SubdivideMeshNode
- primitives: ConeMeshNode, CylinderMeshNode, DualRadialSegmentNode, GridMeshNode, IcosphereMeshNode, QuadCylinderMeshNode, QuadSphereMeshNode, UVSphereMeshNode
- transform: TransformGeometryNode*

(* also have an ArrayMesh path)

### ArrayMesh-returning nodes (4, including dual-path nodes above)
- modifier: ExtrudeMeshNode, InsetFacesNode
- patch: CoonsPatchNode
- transform: TransformGeometryNode

### Design intent
MESH/context.md line 15: 'Half-edge mesh as the core data structure (O(1) adjacency queries)'. That's about *internal* state for adjacency queries during node evaluation (subdivide, extrude, boolean — all need to walk neighbours). It does not require HalfEdge as the *transport* format between nodes.

## Classification — which nodes need HE internally, which can output AM directly

**Can output ArrayMesh directly (no HE needed at any point):**
- All 8 primitives (cube/cone/cylinder/grid/icosphere/uvsphere/quad sphere/quad cylinder, DualRadialSegment) — construct flat arrays from formulas
- TransformGeometryNode — per-vertex position edits, no topology change
- SpherizeMeshNode — per-vertex position edits
- MirrorGeometryNode — duplicate + flip, no adjacency needed
- Most curve-to-mesh (CurveSweepMeshNode, BiRailLoftNode, BirailLoftMeshNode, CurveToMeshNode) — generate triangle strips/grids from curve samples

**Use HE internally but can return AM:**
- SubdivideMeshNode — needs adjacency to identify edge midpoints, then flattens
- ExtrudeMeshNode — needs face adjacency
- InsetFacesNode — needs face adjacency
- MeshBooleanNode — needs HE for CSG classification
- InstanceOnPointsNode — probably AM-flat already; each instance is a static copy
- SeparateGeometryNode — splits by tag; HE not strictly needed
- AttachToSurfaceNode, ApplyBoneNode — position edits guided by topology

**Truly HE-only:** none identified so far. HE is an implementation detail of certain modifiers; not a necessary transport format.

## Recommendation

**Storage policy: ArrayMesh as the canonical transport format between nodes.** Each node internally uses whatever structure is best for its computation (HE for adjacency-heavy ops, AM for everything else). Output is always ArrayMesh. Nodes that need HE input convert upstream ArrayMesh to HE internally via HalfEdgeMesh.from(ArrayMesh) at the top of evaluate().

Why this over alternatives:

  a) 'Keep as-is, fix viewer only' — puts the conversion burden on every consumer of mesh output (viewer, decomposer, exporter). Smells wrong; user explicitly objected to this.
  b) 'Full migration — HE disappears' — loses O(1) adjacency where nodes genuinely need it (subdivide, boolean).
  c) 'Canonicalize outputs to AM, keep HE internal' — RECOMMENDED. Best of both.

## Migration plan

1. Add HalfEdgeMesh.toArrayMesh() as a one-line wrapper over the already-existing compileSurfaceData() pathway. Or reuse SemanticPatchDecomposer.toArrayMesh(MeshTopology).
2. Walk the 23 HE-returning nodes in priority order:
   a. Primitives first (easiest, no internal HE use) — ~8 nodes.
   b. Position-only modifiers next (transform, spherize, mirror) — ~3 nodes.
   c. Curve-to-mesh builders — ~4 nodes.
   d. Adjacency-using modifiers last — keep internal HE, add AM conversion before return — ~8 nodes.
3. For each migrated node: add a golden-file test that validates AM output has the same vertex count, face count, and Euler characteristic as the prior HE output.
4. Update MESH/context.md to reflect: internal HE for adjacency-heavy ops, canonical ArrayMesh transport.

## Storage format for serialized meshes / DSL result

Separately from the in-memory transport format, the agent persistence question: when a DSL evaluates and we cache or serialize the result, should we store ArrayMesh or HalfEdgeMesh? Given ArrayMesh is smaller and downstream agents (Voyager) consume via OBJ load anyway, **store ArrayMesh**. This matches the transport choice. Serialization to OBJ is already ArrayMesh-flavoured (flat triangle list).
definition-of-done: 1. HalfEdgeMesh.toArrayMesh() exists and is tested. 2. All 23 HE-returning nodes have an ArrayMesh return path. 3. Golden-file tests compare pre/post vertex count, face count, Euler characteristic for each migrated node. 4. Viewer patch overlay works on DSL-generated meshes without per-call conversion in the scene. 5. MESH/context.md updated with the canonicalization policy.
testing-plan: For each migrated node: (1) compile, (2) load its simplest DSL example in the mesh viewer, (3) verify it renders, (4) press P and confirm patch overlay works. Batch regression: run voyage-loop on the existing skull reference, confirm output still matches prior chamfer scores within 1% tolerance.
